stem: Name this muscle on the arm model.
explanation: The arrow points to the brachioradialis, the forearm muscle on the thumb side that starts just above the elbow.

stem: Name the muscle the yellow arrow points to on the thigh.
explanation: The arrow points to the rectus femoris, the quadriceps muscle that runs straight down the front of the thigh.

stem: Name the muscle the yellow arrow points to on the lower leg.
explanation: The arrow points to the tibialis anterior, the muscle on the front of the lower leg beside the shin bone (tibia). It pulls the foot upward (dorsiflexion).

stem: Name this muscle on the upright leg model.
explanation: The arrow points to the gracilis, the long, thin muscle on the inner (medial) side of the thigh.

stem: Name this muscle on the leg model lying on the table.
explanation: The arrow points to the gastrocnemius, the rounded calf muscle that joins the Achilles (calcaneal) tendon.

topic: Muscles of the head and neck
stem: Name this muscle on the head model.
explanation: The arrow points to the masseter, the chewing muscle over the angle of the jaw.
The dark oval at the edge of the fiber is a nucleus. Skeletal muscle fibers have many nuclei pushed to the outside edge.

stem: Name this muscle on the torso model.
explanation: The arrow points to the pectoralis major, the large fan-shaped muscle of the chest.

stem: Name the muscle the arrow points to on the open chest.
explanation: The arrow points between the ribs, to the intercostal muscles, which move the ribs during breathing.

stem: Name the muscle the arrow points to on the torso.
explanation: The arrow points to the external oblique, on the side of the abdomen, with fibers that run downward and toward the midline.
